body.statement: If probability measures on \(\mathbb R\) have characteristic functions converging pointwise to a characteristic function that is continuous at zero, then the probability measures converge weakly to the law having that limiting characteristic function.

source.locator: Probability and Measure, third edition, Theorem 26.3
source.verbatim_statement: Corollary 1. Suppose that μ_n are probability measures with characteristic functions φ_n and that lim_n φ_n(t) = g(t) for each t, where the limit function g is continuous at 0. Then g is the characteristic function of a measure μ which is the weak limit of the μ_n.

attestation.note: Verified against the University of Colorado-hosted scan of Billingsley, Probability and Measure, 3rd ed., Theorem 26.3 and Corollary 1 immediately following it; the corollary is the exact strong formulation used by this node.
